description: Order Authorizing Disposition of Jurisdictional Facilities re RE Papago LLC	under EC26-97.
title: FERC Delegated Order — Docket EC26-97-000: Order Authorizing Disposition of Jurisdictional Facilities re RE Papago LLC under EC26-97.
text:
196 FERC ¶ 62,005

UNITED STATES OF AMERICA
FEDERAL ENERGY REGULATORY COMMISSION

RE Papago LLC							Docket No. EC26-97-000

ORDER AUTHORIZING DISPOSITION OF JURISDICTIONAL FACILITIES

(Issued July 2, 2026)

	On May 18, 2026, RE Papago LLC (Papago BESS) filed an application pursuant to section 203(a)(1)(A) of the Federal Power Act (FPA) requesting authorization for a transaction  whereby Papago BESS TopCo LLC (Recurrent Seller) will sell to Harbert Papago Investors, Inc. (Harbert Buyer) Recurrent Seller’s indirect ownership interests in Papago BESS, which owns and operates a 300 MW battery energy storage system (the Papago BESS Project) in Arizona (Proposed Transaction).  The jurisdictional facilities involved in the Proposed Transaction consist of interconnection facilities, a market-based rate tariff and associated books and records, a Shared Facilities Agreement (SFA) between Papago BESS and RE Papago PV LLC (Papago PV), and an LGIA Co-Tenancy Agreement (CTA) between Papago BESS and Papago PV.

	Papago BESS states that it is an exempt wholesale generator with market-based rate authority, and owns and operates the Papago BESS Project, a 300 megawatt (MW) battery energy storage system in Arizona interconnected with the transmission system owned and operated by Arizona Public Service Company (Arizona Public Service).  According to Papago BESS, the output of the Papago BESS Project is fully committed to Arizona Public Service pursuant to a 20-year tolling agreement that is scheduled to terminate on May 22, 2045.

	Papago BESS states that it has entered into the SFA and the CTA with Papago PV.  Papago BESS represents that pursuant to the SFA, Papago BESS and Papago PV own undivided interests in, and have the right to use, certain shared facilities for electrical transmission, interconnection, communications, and other structures and facilities.  According to Papago BESS, the CTA established the terms and conditions for the sharing of rights and responsibilities under the LGIA between Papago BESS and Papago PV.  Papago BESS states that the Commission has accepted both the SFA and the CTA.

	Papago BESS represents that it is currently a wholly owned direct subsidiary of Papago BESS TE Holdings, LLC (TE Partnership).  According to Papago BESS, the passive Class A membership interests in the TE Partnership are held by JPM Capital Corporation, and the controlling Class B interests in the TE Partnership are held wholly and indirectly by Recurrent Seller.  Papago BESS states that Recurrent Seller is an indirect subsidiary of Recurrent Energy, B.V., which is in turned owned 80% by Canadian Solar Energy Group B.V. (Canadian Solar Energy), a subsidiary of Canadian Solar Inc., and 20% by GRP IV Rose Bidco Ltd (GRP IV Rose).  Papago BESS represents that GRP IV Rose is indirectly owned by a fund that is indirectly managed by BlackRock, Inc., a publicly traded investment management firm.

	According to Papago BESS, after the Proposed Transaction, it will become an indirect, wholly owned subsidiary of Harbert Papago Holdings, LLC, which is owned by two entities: (i) Harbert Power Fund VII, LP (Harbert Power Fund VII): and (ii) HPF VII Parallel Fund, LP. (Parallel Fund).  Papago BESS states that Harbert Power Fund VII is a limited partnership owned by its limited partners.

	Papago BESS states that HPF VII GP, LLC (HPF VII GP), as the general partner of Harbert Power Fund VII, will retain indirect day-to-day control over Papago BESS and its assets.  Papago BESS represents that Harbert Management Corporation (Harbert Management) holds 100% of the voting interests in HPF VII GP.  According to Papago BESS, Harbert Management is an institutional investment manager that is owned and controlled by three private individuals.

	Papago BESS states that Harbert Buyer is affiliated with entities that own or control generation in the United States.  Specifically, Papago BESS represents that Harbert Buyer is affiliated with 1,874 MW of generation in the Southern Company Services, Inc. balancing authority area, 680 MW of generation in the Duke Energy Florida, Inc. balancing authority area, 793.4 MW of generation in the California Independent System Operator Corp. market, 540 MW of generation in the New York Independent System Operator, Inc. market, 648.8 MW of generation in the Southwest Power Pool market, 200 MW of generation in the Midcontinent Independent System Operator (MISO) market, and 150 MW of generation in the Arizona Public Service balancing authority area.  Papago BESS also notes that Harbert Buyer is affiliated with Prairie Rose Transmission, LLC, which owns and operates generator interconnection facilities that are needed to connect a 200 MW wind power project to the transmission grid.

	Papago BESS states that the terms of the Proposed Transaction are set forth in a Purchase and Sale Agreement, pursuant to which Harbert Buyer will purchase from Recurrent Seller 100% of the issued and outstanding membership interests in the TE Partnership, the direct upstream owner of Papago BESS.

	Papago BESS asserts that the Proposed Transaction raises no horizontal market power concerns.  Papago BESS states that the Papago BESS Project is located in the Arizona Public Service balancing authority area, the relevant market for purposes of horizontal market power analysis.  Papago BESS explains that while as a result of the Proposed Transaction, Papago BESS will become affiliated with the Justice BESS Project, which is also located in the Arizona Public Service balancing authority area, the capacity of each of the Papago BESS Project and the Justice BESS Project is fully committed under long-term agreements with non-affiliated third parties.  As such, the Proposed Transaction will have no adverse effect on horizontal competition.

	Similarly, Papago BESS states that the Proposed Transaction raises no vertical market power concerns.  Papago BESS states that the Proposed Transaction does not raise any competitive concerns with regard to vertical market power because neither Papago BESS nor Harbert Buyer (nor Harbert Buyer’s affiliates) own or control any of the following inputs to power production: (i) intrastate natural gas transportation, intrastate natural gas storage or distribution facilities; (ii) electric transmission facilities (other than the interconnection facilities necessary to interconnect generation with the transmission grid, in the case of Prairie Rose Transmission); (iii) physical coal supply sources; or (iv) access to transportation of coal supplies, including facilities for the transportation of coal supplies such as barges and rail cars in the relevant it or anywhere else in the United States.  Papago BESS also represents that the Proposed Transaction will not result in any combination of ownership of, or control over, any inputs to generation that could be used to erect barriers to entry into any market.  As such, the Proposed Transaction will have no adverse effect on vertical competition.

	Papago BESS states that the Proposed Transaction will have no adverse effect on rates.  Papago BESS states that the Proposed Transaction will not have any adverse effect on rates for wholesale power sales because all electricity sales by Papago BESS before and after consummation of the Proposed Transaction are and will continue to be made at market-based rates.  Papago BESS represents that while Prairie Rose Transmission provides service to its affiliate Prairie Rose Wind, LLC (Prairie Rose Wind) pursuant to the Prairie Rose Transmission Service Agreement, that service is limited to owning and operating the interconnection facilities necessary to deliver the output of Prairie Rose Wind’s wind power project to the MISO-controlled transmission system, and the rates for service are limited to Prairie Rose Transmission’s costs of operating and maintaining the interconnection facilities.  Accordingly, the Proposed Transaction will have no adverse effect on rates.

	Papago BESS asserts that the Proposed Transaction will not impair the effectiveness of regulation.  According to Papago BESS, the Proposed Transaction does not involve or have any impact on the Commission or any state regulatory authority to regulate Papago BESS or any of its affiliates.  Papago BESS affirms that after the Proposed Transaction is consummated, the Commission will continue to exercise the same jurisdiction it currently exercises over Papago BESS and its jurisdictional facilities and wholesale sales of electricity.  Papago BESS also notes that the Proposed Transaction will have no impact on state commission regulation and the consummation of the Proposed Transaction does not require any order from a state commission.  As such, the Proposed Transaction will have no adverse effect on regulation.

	Papago BESS verifies that, based on facts and circumstances known to it or that are reasonably foreseeable, the Proposed Transaction will not result in, at the time of the Proposed Transaction or in the future, any cross-subsidization of a non-utility associate company or pledge or encumbrance of utility assets for the benefit of an associate company, including: (1) any transfer of facilities between a traditional public utility associate company that has captive customers or that owns or provides transmission service over jurisdictional transmission facilities, and an associate company; (2) any new issuance of securities by a traditional public utility associate company that has captive customers or that owns or provides transmission service over jurisdictional transmission facilities, for the benefit of an associate company; (3) any new pledge or encumbrance of assets of a traditional public utility associate company that has captive customers or that owns or provides transmission service over jurisdictional transmission facilities, for the benefit of an associate company; or (4) any new affiliate contract between a non-utility associate company and a traditional public utility associate company that has captive customers or that owns or provides transmission service over jurisdictional transmission facilities, other than non-power goods and service agreements subject to review under sections 205 and 206 of the FPA.

	The filing was noticed on May 19, 2026, with comments, protests, or interventions due on or before June 8, 2026.  None were filed.

	Information and/or systems connected to the bulk system involved in these transactions may be subject to reliability and cybersecurity standards approved by the Commission pursuant to FPA section 215.  Compliance with these standards is mandatory and enforceable regardless of the physical location of the affiliates or investors, information database, and operating systems.  If affiliates, personnel or investors are not authorized for access to such information and/or systems connected to the bulk power system, a public utility is obligated to take the appropriate measures to deny access to this information and/or the equipment/software connected to the bulk power system.  The mechanisms that deny access to information, procedures, software, equipment, etc., must comply with all applicable reliability and cybersecurity standards. The Commission, North American Electric Reliability Corporation or the relevant regional entity may audit compliance with reliability and cybersecurity standards.

	When a controlling interest in a public utility is acquired by another company, whether a domestic company or a foreign company, the Commission’s ability to adequately protect public utility customers against inappropriate cross-subsidization may be impaired absent access to the parent company’s books and records.  Section 301(c) of the FPA gives the Commission authority to examine the books and records of any person who controls, directly or indirectly, a jurisdictional public utility insofar as the books and records relate to transactions with or the business of such public utility.  The approval of the Proposed Transaction is based on such examination ability.

Section 35.42 of the Commission’s regulations requires that sellers with market-based rate authority timely report to the Commission any change in status that would reflect a departure from the characteristics the Commission relied upon in granting market-based rate authority.  To the extent that a transaction authorized under FPA section 203 results in a change in status, sellers that have market-based rates are advised that they must comply with the requirements of section 35.42.

	After consideration, it is concluded that the Proposed Transaction is consistent with the public interest and is authorized, subject to the following conditions:

The Proposed Transaction is authorized upon the terms and conditions and for the purposes set forth in the application;

Papago BESS must inform the Commission of any material change in circumstances that departs from the facts or representations that the Commission relied upon in authorizing the Proposed Transaction within 30 days from the date of the material change in circumstances;

The foregoing authorization is without prejudice to the authority of the Commission or any other regulatory body with respect to rates, service, accounts, valuation, estimates or determinations of costs, or any other matter whatsoever now pending or which may come before the Commission;

Nothing in this order shall be construed to imply acquiescence in any estimate or determination of cost or any valuation of property claimed or asserted;

If the Proposed Transaction results in changes in the status or upstream ownership of Papago BESS’s affiliated qualifying facilities, an appropriate filing for recertification pursuant to 18 C.F.R. § 292.207 (2025) shall be made;

The Commission retains authority under sections 203(b) and 309 of the FPA to issue supplemental orders as appropriate;

Papago BESS shall make any appropriate filings under section 205 of the FPA, as necessary, to implement the Proposed Transaction; and

Papago BESS shall notify the Commission within 10 days of the date that the disposition of jurisdictional facilities has been consummated.

This action is taken pursuant to the authority delegated to the Director, Division of Electric Power Regulation - West, under 18 C.F.R. § 375.307 (2025).  This order constitutes final agency action.  Requests for rehearing by the Commission may be filed within 30 days of the date of issuance of this order, pursuant to 18 C.F.R. § 385.713 (2025).

								Amery S. Poré, Director
								Division of Electric Power
									Regulation - West
